— The Chapter of the Nazo- —
89   raean who inquires of the Teacher   89
Once again, it happened on a certain time, a Nazoraean came up in the midst
before the Apostle. He said to him: 'I shall ask you a sa-
ying. Persuade me yourself with a single word,
not in many words of his.'
The Apostle said to him:
'{5} indeed{6} you are able to bring forth to me a single word, then I
{7} too shall bring forth to you a single word. But if
{8} you can question me on many, then I myself also shall bring forth to you
a multitude.'
Said that Nazoraean to the Apo-
stle: 'Your God to whom you pray — do you have faith in
{9} truly, or no?'
Then said the Apo-

rean said to him: "For we see that there is no judge
of a city who does not do evil; since every place where a judge
{1} is, there is a whip there wherewith he beats the men
{2}; there is a punishment-rod wherewith he punishes them, among
them; there is a collar attached to him wherewith he sets (it) upon them;
the sword too, wherewith he kills (them) with it. The judge
does all these in the city; but all these are wickednesses.
{3} you see that the judge is an evildoer."
The Apostle said to him in turn: "{4} an associate-of-wickedness
is the judge; but his work is the release of wickedness{5},
casting away the evil. But that which you have proclaimed, that the judge
beats and punishes and slays and {6} — he does
this in this manner: that he is shattering the evil and severing
the evil from the {7}, and laying it upon the head of the sin-
ner. Indeed then, attend through this: that you find a multi-
tude of free, good men who are beside the
tribunal of the judge; and he does not sin against them, {8} does he
draw their account. They themselves have no fears toward him, {9}
{10} they have not sinned. And he himself does not turn upon those
among them; but at the time when one shall do a wicked-
ness against those whom he has sinned against, they seize him and bind him {11}
before the judge. He brings his sin and his {12}
upon his own head. Be filled out then and see, that
the evil does not come from the judge, neither do they call
him a sinner; but the doer of wickedness, {13}
places his own wickedness upon his own head. He who has done {14}
that which is established with the goodness, he also fills himself with the recompense{15}
of the goodness which he has done.
This is the manner also
of God: he too is a Judge of the souls {16}

rather, it is they themselves alone (who) are their works that abide {8}, they are,
those which they habitually appoint, and they shall cast them into the Gehenna of the burning.
These also, who are in the practice of providential nourishment — those (yonder), ac-
cording to their providence-service, He recompenses them with providence-service; He {9}-

ht{11}, and renders them inheritors in the life unto e{12}rnity.

does no evil; rather, his works (are): to render unto the evil one (his due), to bring (him) low in
the midst.
